input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer to Vendor of 15% of annual Fees for each week an invoice is late — a compounding charge triggered by a minor breach (a ten-day payment delay) that within about seven weeks would exceed the entire annual contract value. That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees). No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, minimum-fee or shortfall charges appear: Section 9.4 allows termination without cause with only accrued Fees owed, and Section 27 confirms termination without penalty. We propose deleting the liquidated damages mechanic and substituting simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts as Vendor's sole remedy.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment; replace with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us — 15% of annual Fees per week of delay far exceeds any conceivable loss and would quickly outstrip the contract value. Our position is no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties, so we have replaced this with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts.

ops.newText: 7.7 If a proper, undisputed invoice remains unpaid more than thirty days after its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until payment. Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar stipulated amount under this Agreement.
